title: delete(batch) hygiene change in spawn_fx_predict has no test (NONE coverage)
evidence:
pp.step(&shadow, tt, batch[:], cat)
		delete(batch) // per-tick scratch; temp-allocator frees are no-ops today, but the delete keeps this correct under a tracked allocator (review r1: an earlier comment misclaimed the leak report saw this)
detail: The third behavior change (per-tick batch delete) is traced to no test; it is a no-op under today's temp allocator, so the tracked-allocator contract it establishes is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add a leg that runs spawn_fx_predict with context.allocator swapped for a tracking allocator (or assert via a failing-alloc probe) so the batch-free contract is exercised, or accept and document as untestable hygiene.

title: 14 of 57 alias pins are vacuous in-fixture: skip-on-empty guard bypasses health.*/era_gate.* pins
detail: Fixture never sets health_enabled/advance_gate_enabled; health_make pre-allocates len-0 arrays (health.odin:72-80), so the 9 health + 5 era_gate pins silently skip. A removed clone line for those 14 is caught only incidentally by teardown double-free abort, not by the named pin.
recommended_fix: Skip only truly-nil headers (if len(a) == 0 && cap(a) == 0 { return }), or enable health + advance gate in the fixture so all 57 pins have non-empty buffers and can actually fire.

title: Advisory test gate: PASS
detail: P0 (crash-fix path) 100%: both clone lines pinned by test_spawn_fx_shadow_clone_box_owns_every_array (57/57 Run_State dynamic arrays, verified 1:1) plus the economy leg; RED-before-fix empirically proven (reverting the 2 lines fails exactly the 2 new tests with bad-free reports) and GREEN verified (117/117). P1 ~90%, overall ~90%: sole fully-uncovered change is the no-op-today delete(batch); alias-gate vacuity for 14 empty arrays is backstopped by teardown abort.
recommended_fix: Raise to a clean PASS with zero caveats by covering the tracked-allocator batch contract and de-vacuuming the health/era_gate pins (non-nil skip condition or enabled subsystems in the fixture).
